_source: AI-researched NEW DISTRICT candidates for Manchester and Cheshire, awaiting review — never directly promoted by the research agent. Populated by the same daily scheduled research agent as venue-suggestions.json (2026-08, at explicit user request), committed straight to master the same way (see that file's own doc comment for why). Expected to be rare: the research brief (.claude/agents/curia-research-daily.md) treats district suggestions as an occasional finding (a genuinely distinct, not-yet-covered high-end area within Manchester or Cheshire), not a daily quota — most days should add zero entries here. The daily curia-suggestion-review agent (.claude/agents/curia-suggestion-review.md) is the only thing that promotes an entry into the real docs/data/districts.json, behind its own pull request. Each entry mirrors docs/data/districts.json's own raw shape (name/metro/lat/lon/base/kind/accentColor/editorialDescription) so an approved entry can be copied straight in, plus review-only fields (suggestedDate, status, researchNotes) stripped on promotion. `metro` must be 'manchester' or 'cheshire' only — never 'los-angeles' or a new metro (out of scope, per the user's explicit 'shouldn't go beyond cheshire and manchester just yet').
_reviewWorkflow: Same as venue-suggestions.json: status starts 'pending', the review agent flips it to 'approved' (then copies fields into districts.json, as part of its own PR) or 'rejected' (kept here with researchNotes so it isn't re-suggested). A human's real review happens by reading/merging that PR.

suggestions.name: Macclesfield
suggestions.editorialDescription: The town that funded Prestbury's church and Alderley Edge's stone before either of them meant much — a royal charter in 1261, silk mills worked since into flats and museums both, and streets steep enough that the postcards apologise for them.
suggestions.researchNotes: A genuinely distinct, well-known Cheshire market town not meaningfully covered by any existing district — Prestbury (added 2026-09-03) is explicitly a satellite village whose own character is defined in this file's own copy as downstream of 'the silk money' Macclesfield made, sitting a real 3 miles away (confirmed via rome2rio), a larger separation than several already-accepted close district pairs in this file (Heaton Moor/Stockport Underbanks a few hundred metres, Didsbury/Chorlton ~2.5km). Macclesfield itself is a proper working town centre, not a village green — Market Place (own royal charter, 1261, from the future Edward I, confirmed via multiple historical sources), a genuine silk-manufacturing heritage (Silk Museum, Paradise Mill, West Park Museum, the Old Sunday School, run by the independent Macclesfield Silk Heritage Trust), Georgian and Victorian streets, and a real independent food/drink scene distinct from Prestbury/Knutsford's (The Forest Distillery, Flour Water Salt bakery, MASH, Suburban Bar & Restaurant, per visitcheshire.com). Passes the 'would a local raise an eyebrow' test — a Cheshire local would consider it an obvious gap that Prestbury, Alderley Edge and Knutsford are covered but the town whose silk wealth built much of that same corner of Cheshire isn't. Coordinates are the real Market Place centroid (53.2611/-2.1257, St Michael and All Angels overlooking it), within the existing lat 53.0-53.6/lon -2.6--2.0 sanity box. accentColor (#4F6B63, a muted verdigris/mill-green) chosen for perceptual distinctness against every existing Cheshire accent, all of which sit in the gold/amber/terracotta/rust-brown/olive/plum family — a cooler, industrial-heritage tone reads apart from all of them without leaving the closed warm-adjacent palette CLAUDE.md's Design tokens section governs. base (58) is a reasoned estimate, pending real curation, set a little above Knutsford's (54) given Macclesfield's larger year-round commercial activity as an actual town rather than a market town on a market-day rhythm — same estimation approach already used for Prestbury/Cheadle Hulme/Knutsford. No venues seeded yet — same starting point every prior district promotion has had before its own first venue pass.
